name: Aurora Archipelago - world layout
units: studs (1 stud = 0.3 m), +Y up, map view +X east/right, -Z north/up. Same axes as Lantern Grove / Sugarloaf Canyon.

bounds.note: Terrain extent (1320 x 1320). Far island rings, the cloud sea and the sky sit outside it.

placement_convention.apply: For every (future) holes.json element of hole N: rotate its LOCAL x/z about +Y by placement.yaw_deg, then translate by placement.origin. x' = lx*cos(yaw) + lz*sin(yaw) + origin.x ; z' = -lx*sin(yaw) + lz*cos(yaw) + origin.z ; y' = ly + origin.y. Piece yaw_world = piece.yaw + yaw_deg. Positive yaw = counter-clockwise in the map view: yaw 0 plays north, 90 west, 180 south, -90 east. Check: yaw 90 turns local -Z to world -X. The local origin is the tee; play is toward local -Z.
placement_convention.roblox: holeRoot = CFrame.new(origin) * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(yaw_deg), 0); partCFrame = holeRoot * localCFrame. Axes rotate only.
placement_convention.concept_footprint: Until holes.json exists each hole is concept.pads: flat boxes in the local frame (x range, z range, y offset from origin.y). The future hole geometry (felt + rails + props within 2 studs) must stay inside them. concept.spans = local z ranges where the hole bridges open sky; the ground is not flattened there.
placement_convention.legacy: holes.json exists (Phase 2): it copies these placements into world_offset/world_yaw; world.json placement supersedes them. Walkways start at the real holes.json cups.

terrain.method: Deterministic heightfield h(x,z) (tools/worldlib.py height_at), evaluated in order: (1) base: the cloud floor, h = base.height (0). (2) regions in list order (islands sorted low -> high so higher islands sit on lower ones where they touch). 'set': d = distance outside the shape (0 inside; shape 'union'/'box'/'capsule'/'circle'), plus the edge wobble sum(amp*sin(2*pi*x/wx+px)*sin(2*pi*z/wz+pz)) clamped at 0; w = 1-smoothstep(d/falloff); h += (height-h)*w. 'hill': h += peak*cos^2(pi/2*q), q = elliptical radius/radii < 1 (snowdrifts and crags on island tops). (3) detail_noise where h > detail_min_y (island tops only). (4) pads: every concept pad box flattened to its y, blended back over `falloff` beyond `margin`; along a declared span strip the blend may never raise the ground (the gap stays open). (5) paths: within width/2+1 of a graded segment h = profile (stairs: profile - stair_bed_drop), blended over `shoulder`; on_hole/bridge/lift/gondola don't grade. (5a) flats: teleport/viewpoint discs flattened to y within radius, blended over falloff. (5b) pad clamp: pad boxes (outside spans) = pad y. (6) water: h = min(h, lagoon/runoff carve profile), banks only out to bank_reach. smoothstep(t) = t^2(3-2t), t clamped to [0,1]. VOID: h < void.terrain_fill_min_y means no terrain at all (air over the cloud deck).

path_rules.segment_types: on_hole (across the hole's own area), walk (<1% grade), ramp (<=10%), stairs (flight: steps x rise, tread), landing (flat), bridge (railed, style ice|aurora; <=5%), lift (vertical cage: start/end = boarding points), gondola (cable car)
path_rules.rails: seg.rails = ['left'|'right'...]: sides that need a railing because the ground drops > rail_drop studs within rail_reach (5.5) studs of the walkway edge (stricter than the recipe's 2.5; left/right relative to walking direction). Bridges: both, always. Railings are chunky snow-capped timber, 3.5 studs (1.05 m) high, with a solid lower board so nothing slips under.

heightmap.mapping: pixel (i=col, j=row) centre -> x = bounds.x[0] + (i+0.5), z = bounds.z[0] + (j+0.5) (row 0 = north edge); y = gray/65535*300; y < 30 = void (no terrain)

lantern_posts.note: Brass lantern on a chunky wooden post, warm #FFB861 PointLight (range 14, brightness 0.8). Posts stand 0.75 outside the walkway edge (on bridges: on the railing posts); the lamp sits on top, nothing overhangs the walkway.

vistas.prompt: First-person VR view at standing eye height from the first tee of a mini golf course on the lowest floating island, looking north. Directly ahead a short straight putting green of soft green felt, framed by chunky snow-capped wooden rails, runs 40 studs to a small offset green behind a big snow-capped boulder with one flat angled face; a tall red flag marks the cup. Brass lanterns on driftwood posts glow warm orange along a cobbled snowy walkway on the right, and a cluster of round penguin-puffin snowpuff figures watches from a snowdrift on the left. Beyond the island's snowy rim the ground simply ends at a 24-stud cliff above a sea of soft lilac-white clouds. Far ahead, rising out of the clouds on its own little island, the Starfrost Spire: an enormous faceted aurora-crystal spire glowing mint to violet from inside, with crystal shards orbiting it, towering into the night sky. Green and violet aurora curtains ripple across the northern sky above it. On the right, higher, a second island with steam rising from turquoise hot springs and frosted palms; in the distance more floating islands at different heights, one with a frozen waterfall. A big soft moon glows low behind the viewer to the left, outside the frame, lighting snow edges lilac. Stylized soft 3D render, cozy and whimsical, same art style and palette as the Aurora Archipelago menu card: chunky hand-made shapes, snow-capped floating rock islands over a lilac-white cloud sea at twilight-night, green and violet aurora ribbons, warm brass lanterns on wooden posts, chunky snow-capped timber railings, translucent glowing ice, soft bloom, original design, no text, no logos, no UI.

High overlook from Skylight Point on the west rim of the highest floating island (the summit, y 222), standing beside a small lantern-roofed gondola station and looking east across the summit plateau. Across the left half of the view, three mini golf holes on snowy ground linked by cobbled walkways with brass lantern posts: nearest, a long par 4 that climbs a ramp to a raised green under the Halo Arch, a huge translucent glowing ice arch spanning the hole; beyond it a green that leaps a narrow crevasse open to the clouds on a shimmering green-violet aurora ribbon bridge, beside a sturdier railed ice bridge; furthest, a round moonstone well bowl ringed with glowing ice crystals. Every green has a tall red flag. Past the summit's cliff edge and lower down, the Icefall Terraces island with great frozen waterfalls pouring off its north rim into the cloud sea. On the right side of the view the giant Starfrost Spire rises out of the clouds on its own island, glowing mint and violet with orbiting crystal shards, and far beyond it, much lower, the reef and lagoon islands with turquoise hot springs and wisps of steam. Green and violet aurora curtains fill the upper sky; snowy pines and snowpuff figures dot the plateau. Stylized soft 3D render, cozy and whimsical, same art style and palette as the Aurora Archipelago menu card: chunky hand-made shapes, snow-capped floating rock islands over a lilac-white cloud sea at twilight-night, green and violet aurora ribbons, warm brass lanterns on wooden posts, chunky snow-capped timber railings, translucent glowing ice, soft bloom, original design, no text, no logos, no UI.

First-person view walking onto the Aurora Skybridge, a long straight railed footbridge with a glowing translucent deck that shifts between mint green and violet like the aurora, chunky snow-capped timber railings on both sides with brass lanterns on every second post. It leaps 130 studs across open sky from a small snowy pinnacle to the Icefall Terraces island ahead, where a carousel canopy with a snowpuff weathervane stands over a mini golf green and a timber bell gantry hung with icicles stands beyond it. Far below the bridge lies the soft lilac cloud sea; a small decorative floating islet with snowy pines hangs in the open sky just left of the bridge's far end, a little below eye level. Further left, in the middle distance, the giant Starfrost Spire rises out of the clouds on its own island, glowing mint and violet with orbiting crystal shards; aurora curtains fill the sky above the terraces, and a lilac twilight glow brightens the far left horizon. Stylized soft 3D render, cozy and whimsical, same art style and palette as the Aurora Archipelago menu card: chunky hand-made shapes, snow-capped floating rock islands over a lilac-white cloud sea at twilight-night, green and violet aurora ribbons, warm brass lanterns on wooden posts, chunky snow-capped timber railings, translucent glowing ice, soft bloom, original design, no text, no logos, no UI.

Aerial three-quarter overview of the whole archipelago from high above the south-east, at night under aurora: a ring of floating snow-capped rock islands at six different heights spiralling up anticlockwise around a central floating island that holds the giant glowing Starfrost Spire. Lowest, in the south-west foreground, a harbour island with a lantern-lit quay, three mini golf holes and a small islet across a gap; a railed glowing ice bridge and a lantern stair climb to the next island, a geothermal island with two steaming turquoise hot-spring lagoons, frosted palms and a geyser; behind it to the east a coral-ice reef island in candy pink, tangerine and mint with a conch islet reached by an ice bridge; then north a frozen shelf with a frozen pond; a slender pinnacle and a long glowing aurora skybridge lead west to a terraced island with great frozen waterfalls pouring into the clouds; highest, in the north-west, the summit island with a translucent ice arch over its final green and a gondola cable sweeping all the way back down to the harbour. Small open-cage lifts cling to the cliffs between islands. Every green has a red flag. The cloud sea glows lilac-white below, more distant floating islands and a pierced ice-arch island on the horizon, a low moon to the south-west.
